classification.difficultyReason: Equate squared lengths in an isosceles triangle, solve for an unknown coordinate and select the root consistent with the supplied diagram.

content.prompt: $\triangle ABC$ is isosceles with $AC=BC$. The coordinates of $C$, $B$ and $A$ are $(3,1)$, $(1,3)$ and $(4,a)$ respectively. Find the value of $a$.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle on coordinate axes without grid or numbered ticks. A lies above B and C in the first quadrant. Ordinary source blue edges and red point markers are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: B=(1,3), C=(3,1), A=(4,a), AC=BC. Preserve the diagram restriction a>1 without printing the calculated coordinate.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied axes, triangle, point markers and labels are visible; no calculated coordinate or length is printed.

answer.short:
$a=1+\sqrt7$.

Use $AC^2=BC^2$ and choose the root with $A$ above $C$.
answer.worked:
Since $AC=BC$, their squares are equal.
$$\begin{align*}BC^2&=(3-1)^2+(1-3)^2\\BC^2&=8\\AC^2&=(4-3)^2+(a-1)^2\\AC^2&=1+(a-1)^2\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$\begin{align*}(a-1)^2&=8-1\\(a-1)^2&=7\\a-1&=\pm\sqrt7\\a&=1\pm\sqrt7\end{align*}$$
The diagram places $A$ above $C$, so $a>1$. Therefore $a=1+\sqrt7$.
